paper.title: Dedicated Schools Grant (DSG) Outturn 2025/26
paper.note: Schools-funding monitor to Schools Forum for noting. Zero treasury content: no CFR, no external borrowing, no PWLB, no LOBOs, no maturity profile, no interest rates, no MRP, no prudential indicators. The one datum that touches our world is the accumulated DSG deficit of £12.509m at 31 March 2026, sitting in an unusable reserve under the statutory override extended to March 2028 — worth logging as a dsg-deficit signal, not worth writing to the S151 about from a Schools Forum paper. Audience is head teachers, not treasurers. No companion papers were listed in the brief and none is referenced. Per PIPELINE.md this is the 'schools funding monitor' case — write the note recording exactly that and draft nothing.

facts.value: Total budget £149.849m (after academies and high needs block recoupment); total expenditure £160.797m; in-year DSG pressure £10.948m; prior year balance b/fwd £1.561m; accumulated DSG deficit £12.509m at 31 March 2026 (subject to external audit, and prior to any DfE early-years adjustment).
facts.note: Column footings all tie: 149.849 + 160.797 → variance 10.948; 10.948 + 1.561 → 12.509. Reconciled to Appendix 1 line-by-line.

facts.value: £12.509m accumulated DSG deficit at 31 March 2026, held in an unusable reserve under the statutory override which continues until March 2028.
facts.note: Standard England-wide statutory override under the Local Authorities (Capital Finance and Accounting) (England) Regulations. Signal code dsg-deficit per RECORD_SCHEMA.md. Sits alongside Oxfordshire's -£160.000m DSG unusable reserve as one of the growing sector cluster.

facts.value: Subject to DfE approving a local SEND Reform Plan, the Authority will be eligible for a High Needs Stability Grant in 2026/27 covering up to 90% of the accumulated deficit at 31 March 2026. Residual 10% (~£1.250m on £12.509m) to be funded from the Council's own resources — a General Fund pressure once the override ends.
facts.note: 10% of £12.509m = £1.2509m, ties to the ~£1.250m the paper quotes. This is the emerging DfE settlement pattern for authorities that produce an approved SEND Reform Plan.

facts.value: Expenditure on non-maintained / independent placements (Appendix 1 line 1.2.3): 2023/24 £9.613m → 2024/25 £13.311m → 2025/26 £17.731m. +84% over two years. In-year 2025/26 pressure on this line alone £7.131m; overall high needs block pressure £12.008m; increase in the block's pressure since 2024/25 £7.375m. Paper's own words: 'This level of pressure is financially unsustainable.'

£1.536m Cabinet-approved capital investment to repurpose the former Parr Library site to accommodate additional pupils at Mill Green Special School — expanding in-borough SEND provision that is materially cheaper than out-of-borough independent placements.
facts.note: Capital number, not treasury; recorded because it's the one cash amount in the paper that is being spent (not accrued as a deficit).

facts.value: Not stated in the report. No author byline, no S151 named, no officer email address published. The audience for this paper is Schools Forum members (head teachers and unions), not the S151.
facts.note: Recommendation is 'notes the content of the report' — no decision sought and no responsible officer named. Do not guess.

signals.headline: £12.509m accumulated DSG deficit at 31 March 2026, under the statutory override that continues until March 2028
signals.why_it_matters: St Helens joins the growing sector cluster carrying material DSG deficits below the line; the 90% Stability Grant route (conditional on an approved SEND Reform Plan) would leave ~£1.250m for the General Fund to absorb when the override ends.

summary.text:
St Helens' Dedicated Schools Grant Outturn 2025/26, to Schools Forum on 16 July 2026 for noting only, is a schools-funding monitor and carries no treasury content whatsoever — no CFR, no external borrowing, no PWLB, no LOBOs, no maturity profile, no interest rates, no MRP, no prudential indicators. The audience is head teachers and unions, not the S151. Per PIPELINE.md's rule for revenue outturns and schools-funding monitors, this is a thin note by definition and no email is drafted.

The headline is a £12.509m accumulated DSG deficit at 31 March 2026: a £10.948m in-year pressure on top of a £1.561m prior-year carry-forward. All of it is driven by the high needs block (£12.008m in-year pressure), and within that by non-maintained / independent SEND placements — expenditure on that line alone has risen from £9.613m in 2023/24 to £17.731m in 2025/26, +84% in two years, and the paper describes the level as 'financially unsustainable'. Every internal footing in Appendix 1 ties, including the composition of the £12.008m and the ~£1.250m residual (10% of £12.509m).

The one point of contact with our world is the statutory override under the Local Authorities (Capital Finance and Accounting) (England) Regulations, which continues to March 2028: the deficit sits in an unusable reserve and does not currently hit the Council's revenue budget. Subject to DfE approving a SEND Reform Plan, St Helens will be eligible for a High Needs Stability Grant in 2026/27 covering up to 90% of the accumulated deficit; the residual ~£1.250m becomes a General Fund pressure the Council must identify. This is the emerging sector pattern and we log St Helens' £12.509m alongside Oxfordshire's -£160m 'Unusable DSG Reserve' and the other authorities on the same route.

For completeness — and NOT claimed against this paper — St Helens has a live PWLB book. Our price book holds 20 loans totalling £139.48m at a weighted 3.61% at 31 March 2026 for the correctly-named borrower 'ST HELENS BOROUGH COUNCIL' (note the period after 'St' returns empty in price_book.py --find). No email is drafted from this paper; St Helens goes back into the queue for a Treasury Management Strategy, Mid-Year Review, Annual Outturn Report, or Cabinet-level revenue monitoring paper that surfaces the DSG residual as a General Fund pressure.

contacts.note: Not stated in the paper. Recommendation was 'notes the content of the report' with no responsible officer named. Do not guess an S151 or Director of Finance from a Schools Forum paper.

status.note: Read in full: DSG Outturn 2025/26 to Schools Forum, 16 July 2026 (doc_id 179964). Zero treasury content — schools-funding monitor with a single interesting datum (£12.509m DSG deficit, statutory override to March 2028, up to 90% covered by the emerging High Needs Stability Grant subject to a SEND Reform Plan). Every internal footing ties. Loan-book reconciliation run for completeness (20 PWLB loans, £139.48m, 3.6080% at 2026-03-31 for 'ST HELENS BOROUGH COUNCIL') but there is nothing in a DSG paper to reconcile it against. Balance-sheet identity not applicable — DSG deficit sits in an unusable reserve, not on the borrowing side. Per PIPELINE.md 'only when a paper carries no treasury content whatsoever — a revenue outturn, a planning briefing, a schools funding monitor — write the note recording exactly that and draft nothing.' Officer contact not recorded because Schools Forum audience is head teachers, not the S151, and the paper carries no author byline or officer address. Revisit St Helens when a Treasury Management Strategy, Mid-Year Review, Annual Outturn Report, or Cabinet-level budget monitoring paper reaches the queue — the live 20-loan PWLB book would give a real hook against the right paper.
